primary.$description: The baseline container. Used for high-level structural components like main content sheets,  and primary views. It serves as the standard canvas for the application’s core functional areas

subtle.$description: The contextual divider. Used to signal a shift in environment or to partition secondary content. Apply this when moving into sub-sections like Settings, sidebars, or nested views where a visual layering helps the user understand they are in a different branch of the app

primary.$description: The default color for high importance text, including headings, titles, and primary body copy. Designed for maximum legibility against all standard surfaces.

secondary.$description: Used for supporting text such as captions, metadata, and labels. It reduces visual density to help users scan information quickly.

disabled.$description: Indicates non-interactive content. It strips the visual weight from labels and icons to show they are currently unavailable for user input.

inverse.$description: Applied exclusively to dark or brand-colored backgrounds. Essential for maintaining contrast on Brand background, Surface Inverse, and any   surface requiring negative contrast polarity

primary.$description: The Structural Standard. Provides clear definition for cards, input fields, and main content containers. It ensures elements are distinct without creating excessive visual noise.
